questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
questions.problem:
Find the exact value of $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{12}).$

*Hint: Use the fact that $-\frac{\pi }{12}=\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{3}.$*
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the exact value of $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-{105}^{∘}).$

*Hint: Use the fact that $-{105}^{∘}={45}^{∘}-{150}^{∘}.$*
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $x={45}^{∘}$ and $y={150}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-{105}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘}-{150}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{150}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{150}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{-\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the exact value of  $\operatorname{cos}⁡{195}^{∘}.$

*Hint: Use the fact that ${195}^{∘}={135}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}.$*
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for cosine with $x={135}^{∘}$ and $y={60}^{∘}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡({195}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡({135}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})\cdot \frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the exact value of $\cos \left( -\dfrac{\pi}{12} \right).$

*Hint: Use the fact that $-\dfrac{\pi}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{6} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}.$*
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x - y) = \cos{x}\cos{y} + \sin{x}\sin{y}
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $y = \dfrac{\pi}{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Express $\cos(x - 60^\circ)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(u - v) = \cos{u}\cos{v} + \sin{u}\sin{v}
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u = x$ and $v = 60^\circ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{60}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
canonical_examples.problem: Express $\cos\left( x - \dfrac{\pi}{2} \right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(u - v) = \cos u \cos v + \sin u \sin v
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u = x$ and $v = \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 0+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
